title: Canada Deported Over 3,300 Indians in First Half of 2026, Topping All Nationalities
excerpt: India has overtaken Mexico as the largest source country for immigration removals from Canada, with deportation figures already nearing the full-year 2025 total.
body:
• Canada deported 3,323 Indian nationals between January and June 2026, making India the top nationality for removals for the first time since 2020
  • The six-month figure is already 88% of the 3,779 Indians deported in all of 2025, which was itself a record high
  • An additional 7,669 Indians are in Canada's "removal in progress" inventory, the largest group of any nationality
  • India overtook Mexico, which had 1,573 removals in the same period after leading the list for five consecutive years
  • Canada deported more than 2.5 times the number of Indians removed by the United States during a comparable timeframe

India Tops Canada's Deportation List

Canada removed 3,323 Indian nationals in the first six months of 2026, making Indians the largest nationality group subject to deportation from the country, according to data from the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) reported by The Business Standard and multiple Indian outlets.

The figure has already reached approximately 88% of the 3,779 Indians deported during all of 2025 — itself a record high. If the first-half pace continues, 2026 is on track to set a new annual record for Indian deportations from Canada, according to Madhyamam Online.

India overtook Mexico, which had led Canada's deportation list for five consecutive years from 2021 to 2025. Mexico recorded 1,573 removals in the first half of 2026, followed by Haiti with 431, according to multiple reports.

A Rapid Escalation

The numbers reflect a dramatic acceleration over the past five years. According to Madhyamam Online, deportations of Indian nationals from Canada have risen steadily: 603 in 2021, 786 in 2022, 1,132 in 2023, 2,004 in 2024, and 3,779 in 2025. The first-half 2026 figure already exceeds the full-year total for every year between 2021 and 2024.

Canada's deportation of Indian nationals is also running well ahead of the United States. The U.S. deported 1,273 Indians through July 2026, according to The Business Standard — meaning Canada removed more than 2.5 times as many Indians during a comparable period.

"As of 30 June 2026, 7,669 Indians were in the removal in progress inventory, the largest group among all citizenships."

— Canada Border Services Agency data

Criminality and Enforcement Factors

While the CBSA does not provide a nationality-wise breakdown of removal reasons, the agency has identified criminality and organized crime as significant factors in some Indian removals, according to The Business Standard.

The CBSA flagged Indian nationals on study and work permits as participants in organized criminal activities, including extortion-related violence involving gangs such as the Lawrence Bishnoi outfit. More than 13,040 criminal charges were laid against Indian study permit holders in 2024 alone, while between 2019 and 2023, approximately 4,000 Indians on study permits faced nearly 18,000 charges, the report noted.

Common grounds for removal include visa overstays, rejected asylum or refugee claims, failure to comply with immigration requirements, and visa fraud, according to Madhyamam Online.

Canada Tightens Immigration System

The surge in deportations comes as Canada implements broad reforms to its immigration framework. The government has introduced stricter study permit requirements, greater scrutiny of applications, and a push to reduce temporary resident numbers.

Canada's appeal among Indian students has declined sharply as a result. Indians accounted for just 8.1% of incoming international students in September 2025, down from 51.6% in 2023, according to Canada's auditor general data cited by Madhyamam Online. Indian government figures show the number of Indian students choosing Canada fell 41%, from 233,532 in 2023 to 137,608 in 2024.

What's Next

With 7,669 Indian nationals still in Canada's "removal in progress" inventory — the largest group of any nationality — deportation numbers are likely to continue climbing through the second half of 2026. The pipeline suggests Canada's enforcement machinery is far from done processing the backlog.

For the Indian diaspora community in Canada, the data underscores the risks facing temporary visa holders and the consequences of Canada's immigration overhaul. The trend has also drawn attention in India, where it has become part of a broader conversation about the risks and declining appeal of Canadian immigration pathways.
nri_angle: The surge in deportations directly affects Indian nationals in Canada, many of whom went on study or work permits, and raises urgent questions for the broader diaspora community about immigration pathways.
